title: Dynamic kernel probing playbook for attention stacks
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a practical playbook and lab log for running dynamic kernel probing experiments across our attention serving paths. Aim: establish lightweight, reproducible probes that expose when kernel switching (FlashAttention vs paged/fused ops) improves/worsens 99th/95th latency and per-token cost, and to capture transient failure modes (jitter, microbursts, warmup stalls).

Background/context:
- Observed intermittent 99th-percentile spikes on medium-seq (256-512) mixed workloads.
- Hypothesis space: (1) kernel selection misfires under small-batch bursts; (2) KV cache hot/cold transitions cause prefetch thrash; (3) fused-op variants are sensitive to alignment & padding.
- We need probes that are cheap to run on CI and also a path to reproduce on a dedicated dev rig (A100 80GB node).

High-level approach:
1) Lightweight synthetic traces to exercise decision boundaries: seq-length sweeps, batch-size microbursts, interleaved long/short requests.
2) Deterministic kernel-force runs: force FlashAttention, force Paged, force FusedOp variant X to measure delta.
3) Telemetry capture: per-request timeline (enqueue, schedule, kernel start, kernel end, postproc), memory residency (KV size live), and GPU kernel counters (sm_efficiency, l2_hit_rate, dram_throughput).
4) Interpret with cost-normalized metrics: tokens/sec, p99/p95 latency, per-token GPU ms, and tail-cost (estimated $/1M tokens).

Hardware and software stack:
- Dev rig: 1x A100 80GB, Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS 12.1, Triton runtime pinned to commit abc123, runtime branch: feature/dyn-kernel-probe.
- Models used: llama-2-13b-chat (fp16), stable test prompt set (mix of 8K prompts, see linked PR).
- Runtime flags: --kv-cache-enabled, --batch-coalesce=on, --kernel-prefetch=adaptive (disabled when forcing paged).

Experiment recipes (repeatable):
A) Sequence-sweep microbench
- Purpose: find sequence lengths where kernel switch occurs and measure latency delta.
- Input: 64 requests batch, uniform tokens N in [16,32,64,128,256,384,512,1024].
- Commands: ./run_probe --model llama2-13b --seq N --batch 64 --force-kernel=auto | tee sweep_N.log
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99, kernel chosen, GPU time (ns), l2_hit_rate.
- Notes: enable additional run with --force-kernel=flash and --force-kernel=paged for comparison.

B) Microburst stress (mixed batches)
- Purpose: emulate PG traffic: steady low-latency baseline with occasional 1-2ms spike of high concurrency.
- Input pattern: 30s low load (batch=8, seq=64), then 2s burst (simultaneous 200 requests, seq mix). Repeat 15 times.
- Measurements: queue-length histogram, handoff time between kernels, stall occurrences (kernel schedule >10ms).

C) Fused-op alignment sensitivity matrix
- Purpose: test fused-op numeric/codegen vs padding/alignment.
- Sweep dims: hidden-size mod 32, head count variations, and tile-size choices.
- Run: generator that pads/trims tensors to target alignments and logs fused-op path taken.

Telemetry and lightweight instrumentation plan:
- Request timeline: inject a small tracing span id per request and log timestamps at: enqueue, pre-schedule, kernel-launch, kernel-complete, response-serialize.
- Kernel metadata: kernel-id, grid dims, shared mem used, sm_efficiency (from nvprof/nvmetrics), l2/dram counters.
- Aggregation: produce per-minute heatmaps: chosen kernel vs seq-length vs average batch.
- Storage: local jsonl logs for experiments, upload to s3://lab-rt-probes/<run-id>/ for long-term analysis.

Quick findings (lab notes):
- Sweep run 2026-01-12: FlashAttention performs best at seq <=128 for large single-batch (batch>=32). At seq 256-512, FlashAttention sometimes switches to a fallback kernel due to register pressure—observed increased sm_efficiency variance and 3–8% higher p99.
- Microburst run 2026-01-19: under bursts the kernel selection signal lags behind queue-state changes; we observed a 120–220ms window where the runtime scheduled paged kernels despite median seq being in Flash range—root cause likely stale heuristics that sample only at schedule time.
- Fused-op matrix 2026-01-25: a subset of (hidden_size % 64 == 16) patterns triggered slower fused paths due to unaligned vector loads. Padding to next multiple removed the regression but cost increased memory ops; tradeoff not always worth it.

Representative logs and artifacts:
- Example trace snippet (jsonl line): {"ts":"2026-01-19T15:12:01.312Z", "req_id":"r-7382", "kernel":"paged", "seq":256, "batch":64, "kernel_time_ms":4.9, "sm_eff":0.34}
- See run artifacts: s3://lab-rt-probes/dyn-probe-20260119/ and PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/482 for the tracing hooks.

Interpretation and actionable hypotheses:
- Heuristic staleness: kernel selection heuristic uses stale batch/seq samples; consider faster on-path sampling or schedule-time re-eval that uses queue-profile instead of historical stats.
- Warmup priming: FlashAttention kernels show high variance on cold-start; add micro-warmup (no-op runs) for new contexts or keep a lightweight resident primed context for recent hot keys.
- Alignment-aware fused-op fallback: implement a fast check for problematic alignments and prefer a slightly different fused schedule or an alternative kernel that tolerates misalignment with minimal penalty.

Short-term experiments to run (next 2 weeks):
- A) Implement schedule-time sample hook and run microburst profile: measure p99 reduction target >= 15%. (owner: Benji)
- B) Add forced warmup path on new KV keys and benchmark p95 improvement. (owner: Marina)
- C) Create trimmed padded variant generator to test cost of aligning tensors vs leaving them unpadded; output estimated $/token delta. (owner: Ethan)

Longer-term product considerations:
- Expose a per-route kernel policy in Console: auto vs conservative vs flash-optimistic so customers can trade latency vs cost.
- Add observability: kernel switch events on the Console timeline and alerting when switch frequency > threshold.

Open questions / risks:
- Is the increased memory pressure from padding acceptable for Dedicated customers on constrained pods? Need capacity sims.
- Does aggressive priming materially increase unit cost due to wasted tokens? Measure cost/per-priming-cycle.

Appendix: commands and quick helpers
- Generate synthetic mixed-batch trace: python tools/gen_mixed_trace.py --seed 42 --pattern microburst --out trace.json
- Reproduce schedule-time-sample candidate: ./runtime/bin/rt_client --replay trace.json --force-schedule-sample
- Extract kernel counters sample: nv-nsight-cu-cli --metrics sm_efficiency,l2_hit_rate,dram_read_throughput --target-process pid > counters.csv

Notes-to-self: keep experiment ids in the trace file (run_id + attempt) so we can map logs -> s3 runs. Push minimal travis-style CI for the sweep that runs in ~20min on A100 dev node to catch regressions early.

Concluding remark:
This doc is intentionally a mix of lab notebook and playbook. Use it to run quick reproductions; convert stable recipes into infra-level probes once we converge on reliable heuristics.
